text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

WHEAT SALE - South Korea's Daehan Flour Mills Co Ltd said onTuesday it bought 21,000 tonnes of U.S. No.1 wheat from Japanesetrading house Mitsui and Company Ltd. Shipment was set for March 5-April 5 to the port of Inchon.

CORN SALE - Nichimen Corp said on Tuesday it sold 50,000 tonnes of Argentine corn to Malaysia at the end of last year for shipment this April. The Japanese trade house did not reveal the export price.

CORN AND SOYBEAN TENDER - State-owned Taiwan Sugar Corp would tender on Wednesday for a combined shipment of 20,000 tonnes of No.2 or better U.S. yellow corn and 10,000 tonnes of No.2 or better U.S. yellow soybeans, traders said.

BARLEY TENDER - Saudi Arabia is to tender on Tuesday for 1.2 million tonnes of barley from optional origins, European grain traders said. The barley includes 500,000 tonnes to arrive by the end of February and 700,000 by March 30.

WHEAT TENDER - Armenia is seeking about 65,000 tonnes of U.S. hard red winter wheat under the PL 480 program for January 23-February 6 delivery, its U.S. export agent said. Offers are to be submitted on January 15 and will be valid until January 16.
- Slovenia is expected early this week to tender for 40,000 to 50,000 tonnes of Canadian or U.S. wheat, several U.S. exporters said. Arrival was slated for February 28.
- Taiwan will tender this Thursday for about 85,000 to 86,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat for January-February delivery, several U.S. exporters said.

WHEAT TENDER - South Korea's National Livestock CooperativesFederation (NLCF) passed on tenders for 105,000 tonnes of feed wheat due to high prices, traders said. Traders said the tenders were divided into two lots: 52,500 tonnes for arrival on March 5 and 52,500 tonnes for arrival on June 15.
- Pakistan will be tender January 12 for 315,000 tonnes of Australian white milling wheat and U.S. soft white wheat. Shipment was slated for February 1-28.
- The CCC said it seeks up to 30,000 tonnes of U.S. No. 2 or better hard red winter wheat for donation to Bosnia. Shipment is for Jan 25-Feb 20. Offers are due January 7.

WHEAT TENDER - Bangladesh seeks 100,000 tonnes of U.S. No.2 wheat or Australian standard or better Canadian winter red/spring wheat for shipment by February 21, food ministry officials said. Offers are to be opened January 18 and the results announced two to three days later.
SOYBEAN OIL TENDER - The CCC is to tender for 10,370 tonnes of U.S. bulk crude degummed soybean oil for donation to Peru. Delivery was for Feb 3-18. Offerers will be Jan 8.
RICE TENDER - Syria's General Foreign Trade Organisation for Chemicals and Foostuffs is seeking to buy 12,000 tonnes of white rice for March shipment. Results would be Feb 13.

RICE TENDER - The Japanese Food Agency said it would buy about 60,000 tonnes of rice at an import tender on January 9. In a General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade deal in 1993, Japan agreed to open its rice market, pledging to buy 455,000 tonnes of foreign rice in fiscal 1996/97, which ends on March 31.

SOYBEAN MEAL - The Commodity Credit Corp of the U.S. Agriculture Department said it seeks offers from exporters for 2,650 tonnes of 48 percent protein soybean meal for donation to Guatemala. Shipment is slated for between January 30 and February 25, 1997. Offers are due on January 14 at 1400 CST.

MARKET TALK - France has forwarded to the United Nations the first requests for food exports to Iraq under a U.N. pact allowing Baghdad to buy food and medicine with money from oil sales, a French budget ministry official said on Tuesday.
... A license for U.S. trading giant Cargill Inc to export food to North Korea will provide a sorely-needed lifeline to the communist state, a South Korean analyst said on Tuesday.

... Results of a Saudi Arabian barley tender may be known as early as Wednesday, with the European Union and Australia likely to take the lion's share of the business, Canadian grain export sources said. Saudi Arabia on Tuesday was seeking 1.2 million tonnes of feed barley for January and February shipment. Several Canadian grain traders said Canada was not likely to get much of the business because of weather-related loading delays at Vancouver and the lack of barley in port.
